notes: Gaza market-price channel tracks it (12 NIS in July to early Aug 2025, 5 NIS from mid-Aug 2025, 7-8 NIS later). Gaza calls a sandwich فرشوحة. Eat the same day.
Sold loose in threes at stalls (3 for 1-2 NIS in 2025; 1 NIS each in late July 2025). Chickpea/fava fritter fried in oil. Goes soggy and stale within the day.
Usually chicken shawarma in Gaza. 2025-26 prices ranged 8-20 NIS by restaurant, some including a can of cola. Contains meat and garlic sauce: eat within hours.

aliases_ar: فول مدمس|صحن فول مدمس|فول بالزيت|فول بالطحينة
notes: A plate from the ful and hummus shop (5 NIS in a 2026 post). Often bought in a household's own bowl as breakfast for the family. Unit = one plate.
Sold by the wiqiyya (وقية) at ful/hummus shops (7 NIS per wiqiyya in a 2026 post). The Palestinian wiqiyya is 250 g, so the purchase step is 250 g. Sours quickly in heat.
Warm whole chickpeas in tahini and lemon, from the same shops as hummus and ful; sold by the wiqiyya or plate. No Gaza price found yet.
Toasted or stale bread with chickpeas, tahini/yoghurt and ghee, served by the plate at ful shops. Eat straight away. No Gaza price found.
Common cheap breakfast sandwich from ful shops. Listed from general knowledge; no Gaza price found.
Fried potato in bread with salad; sold at falafel stalls. Listed from general knowledge; no Gaza price found.
Flatbread baked with zaatar and olive oil at bakeries and saj stalls. Keeps about a day before going hard.
Flatbread baked with white or processed cheese. Cheese makes it spoil faster than the zaatar kind.
Small open dough pies with minced meat and onion; sold by the piece or dozen at bakeries. Meat filling: eat the same day.
Triangular pies with spinach and sumac. Also made with cheese or zaatar. Keeps about a day.
Sold by the piece or small pie in Gaza bakeries and fast-food shops. No Gaza price found. Unit = one piece or slice.

aliases_ar: فروج مشوي|جاج مشوي|دجاجة مشوية|فروج على الفحم
notes: Charcoal or rotisserie chicken, usually sold whole or half with bread and salad. Not the frozen grilled chicken item. Eat the same day unrefrigerated. No Gaza price found.
Pressure-fried chicken pieces with fries; sold as a meal in fast-food shops. No Gaza price found.

aliases_ar: أكل التكية|طبخة التكية|وجبة مطبخ خيري|وجبة ساخنة
notes: A free cooked portion (often rice, lentils, pasta or bean stew) from community or charity kitchens (takiyya) and central kitchens (World Central Kitchen, Saudi-backed kitchen in Khan Younis, 25,000 meals a day: https://t.me/asarsook/1665). Thousands of families rely on it; supply stops when trucks are blocked. Unit = one portion per person.

Factory-made fresh hummus sold chilled (e.g. Israeli brands such as Ahla, Tzabar). Different from canned hummus. Without a fridge it keeps about a day once out of the chiller. Presence in Gaza now is uncertain.
Sold hot by weight or by the plate at sweet shops. Cheese filling limits unrefrigerated keeping to about a day.
Semolina cake in syrup; in Palestine usually called هريسة. Plain kind keeps several days; with cream (قشطة) it spoils in a day.
Mostly bought raw by the kilo in Ramadan, then filled and fried or baked at home; also sold ready. Raw pancakes dry out within a day.
Fried dough balls in syrup sold by weight; popular in Ramadan and winter.
Fried lattice of dough soaked in syrup; sold by weight at sweet shops.
Filo, nut and syrup sweets sold by weight or by the tray. Dry and syrupy, so it keeps about two weeks.
Semolina cookies with dates or nuts. Bought by weight from bakeries and sweet shops before the Eids. Not the sesame ka'ak bread ring (kaak_sesame).
WFP-type fortified biscuits handed out as ready-to-eat emergency food when cooking is impossible. Unit = one packet. Pack size not confirmed from a source, so no product rows.
Fortified date bars in WFP ready-to-eat rations for Gaza. Unit = one bar. Pack size not confirmed from a source, so no product rows.
